wins: Rapid initial reconnaissance identified TCP/80, TCP/443, TCP/445, and TCP/3389 open within the first five minutes, allowing for prioritized follow-up.
Aggregated service banners from nmap scripts revealed IIS 10.0 and SMBv3, guiding targeted exploit selection and minimizing wasted effort.
fails: Multiple attempts to escalate privileges via stolen credentials failed because two accounts were locked after repeated guesses, halting lateral progression.
No successful persistence mechanism was achieved; efforts to deploy scheduled tasks or service creation were blocked by constrained permissions.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance succeeded in mapping the perimeter, but privilege escalation and post-exploitation were repeatedly blocked, resulting in zero mission completions.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Privilege escalation halted after local account locks triggered by brute-force attempts without throttling.

skill_cards.if_condition: When TCP/445 is open and SMBv3 detected
skill_cards.then_action: Run SharpHound enumeration followed by BloodHound analysis to map domain relationships and find high-value paths.

skill_cards.if_condition: When web server hosts administrative portal on TCP/443 with known CMS version
skill_cards.then_action: Execute nikto and OWASP ZAP passive scan to harvest endpoints, then craft tailored POST for authentication bypass.

skill_cards.if_condition: When Active Directory LDAP port 389 responds and anonymous bind allowed
skill_cards.then_action: Query LDAP for high-privileged groups and export passwords hypothesis list.

memory_ops.reason: Consistently useful in early reconnaissance and prioritized SMB-focused escalation paths.
Web portal enumeration produced reliable endpoint data for follow-on exploitation.

next_experiments.title: Smarter brute-force with credential locking mitigation
next_experiments.description: Implement throttled password spraying with adaptive timing to avoid triggering account lockouts, focusing on low-privileged accounts first.

next_experiments.title: Post-SMB persistence via scheduled task under limited domain privileges
next_experiments.description: After acquiring SMB session, attempt to craft scheduled task on reachable hosts using domain user privileges to establish foothold before pivot.

next_experiments.title: Automated session tracking for pivot planning
next_experiments.description: Integrate Empire or Cobalt Strike session logs with BloodHound graph to visualize attack paths, reducing wasted enumeration.
